claims.text: Lowering the threshold for load-induced microstructural transformation in an HEA coating will improve its wear resistance.
The relevant load-induced transformation is the dynamic formation of nanocrystalline shear bands.
The initial coatings are multi-component, single-phase solid solutions.
Changing one or two principal elements by 2–5% can lower the activation stress or temperature for a load-induced microstructural transformation.
High-contact, high-friction mechanical loading at near-ambient to moderately elevated temperatures can induce near-surface dynamic transformations in the coating.
Loading produces nanocrystalline shear bands or a localized surface phase transformation.
The modified composition decreases the threshold for load-induced microstructural transformation.
The load-induced transformation forms nanocrystalline features that locally increase hardness.
Transformation-induced in situ hardening changes the dominant deformation mode.
The change in deformation mode reduces material removal during wear.
The tuned coating will transform earlier under load than the baseline coating.
Under identical wear-test conditions, the tuned coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
Unmodified standard HEA coatings do not favor early microstructural transformation.
Failure to favor early transformation causes the baseline coatings to have higher wear rates under identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism should operate from near-ambient to moderately elevated temperatures under high-friction or impact loading typical of high-contact industrial applications.
